candidates.context: 2. Review teams will follow the most recent and up-to-date OCP Internal Quality Procedures. 4. Informal meetings and communication among OCP review team members and other discipline reviewers (e.g., clinical, biostatistics, pharmacology and toxicology, chemistry, manufacturing) are encouraged. Because participation in meetings is issue-based, keeping the entire OCP review team informed of key findings is important throughout the review process. Thus, important review findings that might influence approval or labeling decisions should be discussed among the OCP review team to gain alignment prior to engaging with other members of the CDER review team. Relevant outcomes of interactions with other disciplines outside of OCP that may be relevant to the OCP review should be shared with the rest of the OCP review team.

candidates.context: 7. A separate OCP Application Signatory Memorandum will be written when there is major disagreement within the OCP review team that cannot be resolved during review, when the application signatory does not agree with the final recommendations of the review team, when OCP is taking a precedential or controversial review position, or when the complexity of the review issues necessitates further written communication.

candidates.statement: Information should generally not be repeated within the review. Reviewers may refer the reader to relevant sections and use hypertext links where appropriate. Text, tables, and figures may be used to summarize information, but redundancy should be avoided. The approach that best ensures clarity and understanding should be used. Proper attribution regarding data sources and analyses is expected. Reviews should be clear as to which assertions, conclusions, and recommendations are those of the applicant and those of the review team. Coherent and concise writing is expected for all draft and final reviews.
candidates.context: Effective Date: 11/10/26 Page 8 of 18 ATTACHMENT 1: OCP-SPECIFIC ISSUE-BASED REVIEW GENERAL INFORMATION AND TEMPLATE General Information The purpose of the review template is to consistently ensure that critical information is presented by OCP review teams in a prioritized, issue-driven, and logical manner. The template provides standardization and consistency in the format and content of clinical pharmacology reviews and ensures that critical presentations and analyses will not be inadvertently omitted. The standardized structure also enables readers to readily locate specific information. As such, headings and subheadings are named, numbered, and ordered as stipulated in the template unless there is a compelling reason not to for a specific application. The template may be modified by OCP review teams if deemed necessary to ensure clarity and cohesion for a given application; however,

candidates.statement: 2 Summary of Clinical Pharmacology Assessment This section provides an integrated synopsis of the major clinical pharmacology issues dealt with in the course of a typical OCP review of an NDA, BLA, or OMOR. Only topline information should be presented in this section. Additional details are expected to be included in the section 3 Comprehensive Clinical Pharmacology Review.

candidates.context: 3.2 General Pharmacology and Pharmacokinetic Characteristics Include a general overview of the drug’s non-clinical and clinical pharmacology information to provide a context for specific OCP recommendations. Briefly include information on the drug substance (note for BLAs, drug or drug substance means the therapeutic protein, terms which can be used interchangeably), drug product, and bioanalytical method if relevant to an important aspect of the review. Key information may be summarized in a table format. Effective Date: 11/10/26 Page 15 of 18 front.

candidates.context: 3 When final, these guidances will represent the FDA’s current thinking on these topics. 3.3.2 Is the proposed dosage appropriate for the general patient population for which the indication is being sought? Provide an assessment of and final dosage recommendations for the general patient population for which the indication is being sought. This section could also include the details on the dose finding approach as well as the integrative approach taken (including pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, efficacy, and safety information) to support the proposed dosing regimen. If necessary, this section should include revised dosing recommendations to be incorporated into labeling or proposal for further studies to resolve any unresolved issues related to dosing for the indication sought.

candidates.statement: If necessary, this section should include revised dosage recommendations to be incorporated into labeling or proposals for further studies to resolve any unresolved issues related to dosage in specific populations. The basis for alternative dosage recommendations in these populations should be explicitly described (e.g., average exposure matching, interpolation or extrapolation based on exposure-response analyses).
candidates.context: 3.3.3 Is an alternative dosing regimen and/or management strategy required for subpopulations based on intrinsic factors? Provide an assessment of and final recommendations on dosage and/or the appropriateness of treatment in relevant patient subsets based on various intrinsic factors. Intrinsic factors include age, sex, race/ethnicity, genetics, body weight, organ impairment, etc. This section can provide information on:

candidates.statement: • Intrinsic factors that were evaluated or considered but that do not influence exposure should be discussed. The adequacy of the data to support a negative finding should be discussed.
candidates.context: • Whether intrinsic factors were adequately assessed and if such information is pertinent to safe and effective use of the drug. 3.3.4 Are there clinically relevant food-drug or drug-drug interactions, and what is the appropriate management strategy? Provide assessment of and final recommendations on dosage and/or therapeutic management strategies needed to address important food-drug (including beverage- drug) or drug-drug interactions. If necessary, this section includes revised management strategies to be incorporated into the labeling or proposals for further studies to resolve such clinically relevant interactions. The basis for alternative dosages under these conditions is explicitly described (e.g., average exposure matching, interpolation or extrapolation based on exposure/response analyses).
